hook: HPV causes oral cancer. Most people don't know.
caption:
Most people associate HPV with cervical cancer. The connection to oral cancer is far less known, and that gap is showing up in diagnosis rates.

About 70% of oral cancers in the U.S. are now linked to HPV, and the fastest-growing group being diagnosed is adults between 35 and 55. These are people who had no symptoms, felt healthy, and had no reason to think an oral cancer screening applied to them.

The tricky part is that HPV-related oral cancer often develops in the back of the throat where it's hard to see and easy to miss. By the time symptoms appear, the disease has usually progressed.

Knowing your risk is the first step. Take the free screener at oralcheck.org to understand where you stand.
